main_text.p: עָנַם Contriftatus, Anxius fuit: Præt. עָגְמָה נַפְשִׁי [?] Anxia erat anima mea, Job.30.25.

עָנַן Niph. נֶעֱנַן [?] Morari, Differre, Detineri. Futurum, תֵּעָנֻנוּ [?] Retardabitis vos ipsas; Morabimini, Differetis, Ruth.1.13. pro תֵּעָנֻנוּ [?]. Hinc apud priscos Hebræos עָנָן [?] vel עָגֹן [?] Anchora; sic dicta, quòd navem Remoratur, ad quam significationem probandam adducitur hic locus ex libro Ruth, apud Talmudicos in Bava Bathra, cap.5. in principio. In Targum, וַיַּעֲגּוּנוּן לְבֵית עֲגָנָה [?] Et detinebant eos in domo detentionis sive carceris, Jef.24. v.22. וּבְבָתֵּי יְסוּרִין עֲגִינְיהוֹן [?] Et in carceribus detinentur illi, Jesa.42. v.22. ubi melius fortasse legi posset עֲגִנִינוּן [?], pro עֲגִין אִנּוּן [?] per compositionem tertiæ personæ Pronominis cum Participio, cujus tamen alia exempla hactenus mihi non occurrerunt.
עָגוּר Hirundo, juxta R.Sal. Jesa.38.14. Jer.8.7. Aliis, Grus, Ardea.

עָדַד Pih. עוֹדֵד Statuminavit. Partic. מְעוֹדֵד עֲנָיִם [?] Statuminans manfuetos, Pfal.147.6. Fut. יְעוֹדֵד Statuminabit; Pfalm.146.9. Hithp. Futur. וְנִתְעוֹדֵד [?] Et erecti confistimus, Pfal.20.9. q.d. statuminati.

עָדָה Ornavit, se vel alium: Et ex significatione Chaldaica, Transivit. Præterit. עָדָה עָלָיו [?] Transivit per eam, Job.28.8. וְעָדִית עָדִי [?] Et ornas te ornatu, Ezech.23.40. Imper. עֲדֵה [?] Orna te, Job.40.10. Futur. וְאֶעָדֵךְ [?] Et ornavi te, Ezech.16. v.11. תַּעֲדֶה [?] Quæ ornat se, Jesa.61.10. unde per Apocopam, תַּעַד [?] Et ornavit se, Hos.2. v.14. Chaldaicè, Transivit, Discessit, Præteriit: Præter. Fœm. עָדַת מִנָּךְ [?] Tranfit, Discedit à te, Daniel.4.28. Futurum, יֵעְדֵּה [?] Præterit, Dan.7.14. Et in א tertia fœmin. לָא תְעַדָּא [?] Non transit, Intercidit, Dan.6. v.8. Hithp. Partic. מְעַדֵּה בְּגָד [?] Ornans se veste, juxta quosdam,

page.notes: Hebrew headwords and Hebrew citations are copied from a small, heavily blurred scan. Vowel points and some consonants are uncertain; each doubtful form is marked [?]. The running head is Hebrew and only partly legible. The last entry ends mid-sentence ("juxta quosdam,"), so the text likely continues on the next page. Latin abbreviations and citation numbers are copied as printed, including "Jef.24." and "Jefa.38.14." (possibly Jes./Jesa. in the printer's usage).
